paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: following Jesus is not a casual stroll with a big crowd. Jesus turns around to a whole parade of people and tells them the truth up front. He says anyone who does not carry his cross and follow Him "cannot be My disciple" (Luke 14:27). He wants them to know what they're signing up for, and I respect that, because I've signed up for plenty of things without reading the fine print.

Then He gives two pictures, a builder and a king, and both of them sit down first and count the cost. The lesson is that Jesus puts Himself first, ahead of family, ahead of our own life, and ahead of everything we have (Luke 14:26, 33). I think He's not trying to scare anybody off. I think He's saying that a half-hearted yes won't hold up, and a whole-hearted one will. Following Him means giving up everything we're holding onto, and that's a big ask, so He asks it out loud.

And that's why the salt matters at the end. Salt is good, but salt that has lost its savor is thrown out (Luke 14:34-35). A disciple is meant to be the real thing, with the flavor still in it. So He closes with "He who has ears to hear, let him hear" (Luke 14:35). Baker, don't just nod along, hear it, count it, and follow Him with all you've got.
